requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Get swatches of two natural fiber fabrics (100% cotton, linen, wool, or silk; no blends). Get swatches of two synthetic fiber fabrics (nylon, polyester, acrylic, olefin, or spandex). Get a sample of one cellulosic fabric (rayon, acetate, or lyocell). (b) Give the origin, major characteristics, and general content of each type of fiber obtained for 2(a). Explain the difference between a cellulosic manufactured fiber and a synthetic manufactured fiber. (c) Describe the main steps in making raw fiber into yarn, and yarn into fabric. (d) Assume you will soon buy a new garment or other textile item. Tell your counselor what fiber or blend of fibers you want the item to be, and give reasons for your choice.

pamphlet_excerpts: Aramid Fibers Increasingly: Aramid fibers are increasingly being used as replacementsfor steel, fiberglass, asbestos, and aluminum.
Skis Aramid-fiber Cores: Skis with aramid-fiber cores lastlonger and perform better.
Racing Drivers Wear: Racing drivers wear aramid suitsthat help prevent them from burning to death in fiery, high-speed crashes.
Carbon Fibers Extremely: Carbon fibers are extremely strong, stiff, lightweight fibersof nearly pure carbon made by “baking” or “charring” rayon, pitch, or acrylic fibers.
step_by_step_procedure: They Tostrengthen Airplanes: They are used tostrengthen airplanes and spacecraft.
Exhaust Nozzles Thetwo: The exhaust nozzles of thetwo large booster rockets that lift the space shuttle into orbitcontain 30,000 pounds of carbonized (charred) rayon.
Threedimensional Fabrics: Threedimensional fabrics made from carbon fibers may somedayreplace steel in such products as automobiles, military vehicles, and building.
Lyocell Produced United: Lyocell, first produced in the United States in 1992, is a relativeof rayon.

requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following: (a) Visit a textile plant, textile products manufacturer, or textile school or college. Report on what you saw and learned. (b) Weave a belt, headband, placemat, or wall hanging using a simple loom that you have made yourself. (c) With a magnifying glass, examine a woven fabric, a nonwoven fabric, and a knitted fabric. Sketch what you see. Explain how the three constructions are different. (d) Make a piece of felt. (e) Make two natural dyes and use them to dye a garment or a piece of fabric. (f) Waterproof a fabric. (g) Demonstrate how to identify fibers, using microscope identification or the breaking test.

Cotton Fiber Instance: Cotton fiber, for instance, lookslike a twisted ribbon under a microscope.
Rough Textureof Natural: The rough textureof natural fibers helps the fibers stay together when they aretwisted into yarns.
Manufactured Fibers Smooth: Manufactured fibers are smooth or havebeen given lengthwise grooves and specially treated to becrimped or twisted.
step_by_step_procedure: Start Threads Pull: Start with threads you pull from the edgeof an identifiable piece of fabric.
Hold Ends Fingers: Hold the ends in your fingers and pull theyarn apart.
Observe Point Breakage: Observe the point of breakage, and compare tothe descriptions that follow.
Aramid Fibers Increasingly: Aramid fibers are increasingly being used as replacementsfor steel, fiberglass, asbestos, and aluminum.

pamphlet_excerpts: Aramid Fibers Increasingly: Aramid fibers are increasingly being used as replacementsfor steel, fiberglass, asbestos, and aluminum.
Skis Aramid-fiber Cores: Skis with aramid-fiber cores lastlonger and perform better.
Racing Drivers Wear: Racing drivers wear aramid suitsthat help prevent them from burning to death in fiery, high-speed crashes.
Carbon Fibers Extremely: Carbon fibers are extremely strong, stiff, lightweight fibersof nearly pure carbon made by “baking” or “charring” rayon, pitch, or acrylic fibers.
step_by_step_procedure: They Tostrengthen Airplanes: They are used tostrengthen airplanes and spacecraft.
Exhaust Nozzles Thetwo: The exhaust nozzles of thetwo large booster rockets that lift the space shuttle into orbitcontain 30,000 pounds of carbonized (charred) rayon.
Threedimensional Fabrics: Threedimensional fabrics made from carbon fibers may somedayreplace steel in such products as automobiles, military vehicles, and building.
Lyocell Produced United: Lyocell, first produced in the United States in 1992, is a relativeof rayon.

Fabric Advertisements: You see fabric advertisements in magazines and newspapersand look at television commercials for items made of fabrics.
Work Done Artists: This work is done by artists and writers who work either forthe textile companies or for their advertising agencies.
Selling Calls People: Selling calls for people who like people, who welcome challenges, who are enthusiastic, and who know the product theysell inside and out.
step_by_step_procedure: Think Qualities Youcould: If you think you have these qualities, youcould think about a career in textile sales, sales management, or marketing.
Textile Companies Training: Many textile companies have training courses forsales representatives.
Careers Textiles Require: Many careers in textiles require college training.
Talk Guidance Teacher: If you are inhigh school, talk to your guidance counselor or a teacher aboutyour ideas for your future.
